How much should you tip valet parking?

Valet tips are flat amounts, not percentages. The standard is $2–5 at pick-up for restaurant or standard hotel valet, and $5–10 for luxury hotels or special events. Tip only at pick-up. This is the universal convention. The attendant receives the full tip when they return your car.

"Free valet" means no parking fee, not no tip. Always tip $2–5 at pick-up even when valet is complimentary. The attendant performed the same service regardless of what you paid for parking.

Factors that affect how much to tip

  • Venue type: Budget hotel or casual restaurant ($2–3), standard hotel or upscale restaurant ($3–5), luxury hotel or formal event ($5–10).
  • Service speed: If the attendant retrieved your car quickly during a busy rush, tip at the higher end. A 20-minute wait during a fully-staffed slow period warrants the standard amount.
  • Special requests: Pulling up early, holding your car close, helping with bags or strollers, all warrant tipping toward the upper range.
  • If you retrieve your car multiple times (e.g., at a hotel over a multi-day stay), tip $3–5 at each pick-up, not just the first and last.

Valet tipping etiquette

Have your tip ready in cash before the attendant brings your car. Fumbling for cash while holding up the line is awkward for everyone. A $5 bill in your pocket before you hand over your keys makes the exchange smooth and intentional.

If the valet damaged your car, report it to the manager immediately and photograph the damage before leaving. You are not obligated to tip for damaged property. File a claim through the company's insurance. Do not accept verbal assurances and drive away.

Frequently asked questions

How much should you tip valet parking?
Tip $2–5 at pick-up for standard restaurant or hotel valet. Tip $5–10 at luxury hotels or special events. Tip only at pick-up, not drop-off — the attendant receives the full tip when they return your car.
Do you tip valet at drop-off or pick-up?
Tip at pick-up only. This is the standard convention — the tip is given after the full service is complete. Some guests tip $1–2 at drop-off and the rest at pick-up, but tipping only at pick-up is perfectly acceptable.
Do you tip valet if the service is free?
Yes. Free valet means no parking fee, not no tip. Tip $2–5 at pick-up even when valet is complimentary — the attendant performed the same service regardless.
How much do you tip hotel valet?
Tip $3–5 at pick-up at a standard hotel. At a luxury hotel or resort, tip $5–10. Tip at each car retrieval during a multi-day stay, not just once.
How much do you tip valet at a restaurant?
Tip $2–5 at pick-up for restaurant valet. At upscale restaurants or for quick service during a busy rush, $5 is appropriate.
Should you tip more for a nice car?
No — tip based on the quality and speed of service, not your car's value. The service performed is the same regardless of what you drive.
Is it rude not to tip valet?
Yes. Valet attendants earn near minimum wage and depend on tips. Not tipping is considered rude, especially given the trust involved in handing over your vehicle.
Do you tip valet at a hospital?
Appreciated but less strictly expected. $2–3 at pick-up is a kind gesture. Some hospital valet services are nonprofit and explicitly decline tips — check on arrival.
Do you tip more for fast retrieval?
Yes. If an attendant retrieves your car faster than expected or handles a special request, tipping at the higher end ($7–10) is appropriate acknowledgment.
What if the valet damages your car?
Report damage to the manager immediately and photograph it before leaving. You are not obligated to tip for damaged property. File a claim through the valet company's insurance.
